mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses in a low-inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during periods of strong export-led growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect is absent during periods of high wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a deceleration in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1 standard deviation from their 12-month moving averages indicates a shift from construction to manufacturing focus, which historically precedes cyclical equity drawdowns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during periods of strong global demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a period of negative core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL excluding food & energy) signals a liquidity trap, which historically coincides with muted equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.5% in one month AND CPIAUCSL (core) < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 delivers positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect is absent when fiscal stimulus is large.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a precautionary savings regime that reduces near-term consumption-driven demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern breaks during periods of strong fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its long-run trend, without a corresponding rise in the unemployment rate, signals labor market tightness that precedes wage inflation and ultimately negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > long-run trend for six consecutive months AND UNRATE stable or falling
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing sector downturn that propagates to broader consumer confidence and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of months when HOUST is below its 12-month moving average for four straight months.
